dataset_family: Ruijin Hospital (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) neurology/memory clinic cohort, 2016-2020: 19 NC, 23 MCI (Mayo/Petersen criteria), 17 AD; controls recruited from the Shanghai community
method_family: Conventional ophthalmic testing (Stratus OCT macular RNFL thickness, flash ERG, pattern VEP) with group comparisons (one-way ANOVA, Bonferroni) and correlation/hierarchical regression against 3T MRI hippocampal volume; no classifier, no discrimination metric
what_it_shows: Zhao et al. 2021, Front Aging Neurosci. In an age-matched single-centre sample, MCI had a thinner macular RNFL than NC (96.76 vs 88.65 um; pairwise P = 0.011, under the Bonferroni threshold of 0.017) and a delayed flash-ERG rod-cone response latency (P = 0.003). m-RNFL correlated with hippocampal volume (partial r = 0.521) and independently predicted ADAS-cog (beta = -0.242, P = 0.031), but not MMSE or MoCA. The results are group-level only: no AUC, sensitivity or classification, no external validation, and scalability is not tested.
why: PDF identity confirmed: title, authors (Zhao, Fang, Li, Chen, Qiu, Wu, Xu, Deng) and DOI 10.3389/fnagi.2020.597491 match the block. I read the whole extract through the references. STATED FORM, partly: the study's own data support the retinal-structure leg (and a retinal-function measure) as a biomarker direction for early cognitive decline, because MCI differs from age-matched NC. It does not test scalability, the authors only assert that the tests are non-invasive and cost-effective, and it reports no detection performance. This matches how round 20 scored P-966. NARROWED FORM, yes: the headline claim is a preliminary, single-centre association of an ocular measure with MCI, and this study's own MCI-vs-NC contrast shows exactly that (m-RNFL P = 0.011; FERG rod-cone latency P = 0.003). The design is age-matched (P = 0.251), which avoids the P-952 age confound. Two scope points. (1) It shows an association, not discrimination, so the sub-clause 'retinal imaging ... discriminated MCI' does not describe it; admitting it would require wording such as 'retinal OCT thickness differed from controls'. (2) It is a third Chinese hospital cohort (Shanghai). Corrections to the finders: the block's 'P<0.001, eta2p=0.393' is the three-group omnibus ANOVA, and the MCI-vs-NC figure is P = 0.011 (p.5 text). One finder said the analysis is by eye, but the PDF averages both eyes per subject (p.4), so the unit is the participant. Caveats: 23 MCI only; clinical MCI without amyloid or tau (the authors concede that specificity to AD cannot be confirmed, p.7); the number of eyes excluded is not reported; the ocular measures were not associated with MMSE or MoCA. Independence: Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai. It shares no site, cohort or authors with P-5 (Daping Chongqing / WMU Wenzhou), P-952 (Sun Yat-sen 7th Affiliated, Shenzhen), P-966 (GARD Korea) or P-105 (review), and none with the other candidates. Not a preprint: peer-reviewed Frontiers article.

quotes.quote: Participants (N = 59) in this study were enrolled at the neurology clinic of Ruijin Hospital affiliated to the Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai, China, from September 2016 to December 2020.
Both eyes for each subject were examined and the average of these measurements was taken for the both eyes.
delayed rod cone response latency time was found in both MCI (P = 0.003) and AD (P = 0.003) patients compared to normal controls.

MCI patients showed significantly thinner m-RNFL compared to normal individuals (P = 0.011) as well. However, no significant morphological changes in the optic disc head were found for the rim area, disc area, and cup volume.

hippocampal volumes (β = −0.490, P < 0.001) and m-RNFL thickness (β = −0.242, P = 0.031) were significantly associated with ADAS-cog scores (Table 4). Regarding scores of MMSE (Table 5) and MoCA (Table 6), however, just the parameter of hippocampal volumes demonstrated strongly positive associations (β = 0.527, P < 0.001; β = 0.664, P < 0.001; respectively), while parameters of ocular indexes revealed no significant association (P > 0.05).

In the current cross-sectional study we have enrolled relatively small sample size, partially due to strict exclusion criteria of patient enrollment and adaptability to full screen of ocular structural and functional measurements. A longitudinal study with expanded sample size is required to validate the retina-brain association in the neurodegenerative process of cognitive decline.

Owing to the lack of Aβ or Tau-related markers, we were unable to analyze the relationship between those pathological markers and ocular measurements, and hence the present findings cannot directly confirm whether the alterations in the ophthalmological examinations are specific to AD.
